newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries higher on dlr's strength in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries higher on dlr's strength in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries edged higher in Tokyo trading on Monday due to light short-covering led by dealers in reaction to the dollar's rise against the yen, traders said.
But prices peaked after the greenback retreated from early highs on profit-taking, they said.
Bargain-hunters were more willing to buy as the yield of the key 30-year bond shot up to around 6.75 percent.
"Besides the factor of the dollar, there is no driving force," a Japanese trust bank trader said. "Tokyo operators seem more eager to buy on dips after the recent (price) falls."
The key 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond was at 97-2/32, yielding 6.73 percent, compared with 97 in New York on Friday.
March T-bond futures contract also rose 4/32 to 111-22/32 from the previous close.

"Prices tumbled rapidly during holidays (in Tokyo). But it's too premature to determine that underlying sentiment had turned bearish," the trader said. "I don't expect the key (30-year) yield to climb sharply above 6.75 percent."
The market participants expect Friday's payroll data to determine near-term trends, but until then Treasury prices are likely to be stuck in a tight range, traders said.
